Speaker: Old Fern
Current line: Shh. Keep it down. Old Fern. Composter.

Speaker: Old Fern
Current line: I turned this city's waste back into soil. Now that's 'untidy', and so am I. Criminally untidy. Worms in my hat to prove it.

Speaker: Old Fern
Current line: They shoved the rubbish behind the facade and called it 'Behind'. The land's sick. Nothing grows. Help me save what's left.

Speaker: Old Fern
Current line: Any luck? The heaps are in cellars and holes all over the Reek. They think they're hiding. They're being rescued.

Speaker: Widow Pell
Current line: Oh. A visitor. Forgive me, I've forgotten how this goes. I am Widow Pell. My husband died three years ago, in his chair in the front parlour.

Speaker: Widow Pell
Current line: I cannot bury him. Form 27-B needs Form 27-C, and 27-C needs 27-B. He has waited in his chair for three years.

Speaker: Widow Pell
Current line: I talk to him in the parlour. He was always the patient one. I'm not, it turns out. Please, if you can help.

Speaker: Widow Pell
Current line: The stamp, remember. Someone hid the Stamp of Final Approval where nobody official would look: somewhere in Grave Row, among papers nobody reads.

Speaker: Rollo Spokes
Current line: Rollo Spokes... foreman. Beefcake. Learned the wheels... in the Gainlands. Back then, a wheel stopped at night.

Speaker: Rollo Spokes
Current line: Now the facade needs light... so we pedal. Free. Forever. We were told... it was cardio. My calves have calves.

Speaker: Rollo Spokes
Current line: My crews run six hours a day... for ten years. Nobody's told them they can stop. Somebody ought to.

Speaker: Rollo Spokes
Current line: Three wheels... pull the brakes. And that big cable by the east wall... feeds the facade. Cut it.

Speaker: Rollo Spokes
Current line: The crews won't stop... till somebody says it's all right. You say it.

Speaker: Chef Marlo
Current line: Hands where I can see them. Good. Chef Marlo. Once of the Market of the Four Paths. Now a 'Nutrient Distributor'. Recipes stay in my apron.

Speaker: Chef Marlo
Current line: Everyone eats {villain}'s Perfect Nutrient Paste, three times a day. Paste is food the way a form is a hug.

Speaker: Chef Marlo
Current line: For ten years I've hidden real recipes all over this quarter, so that somebody, somewhere, remembers what food is.

Speaker: Chef Marlo
Current line: Three recipe cards, hidden in the quarter. And the dispenser: give it a good kick from me. Spoil it. Spoil it badly.

Speaker: Captain Spotless
Current line: HALT. I am Captain Spotless. State your height.

Speaker: Captain Spotless
Current line: No: do not state it. Stand at it. Straighter. Not that straight. APPROVED straight.

Speaker: Captain Spotless
Current line: Entry requires the Approved Visitor Standard. You are too tall. You are too short. Your shadow is the wrong length.

Speaker: Captain Spotless
Current line: However. The Standard has a provision: the Entry Examination. A card battle. Win it, and you are, retroactively, approved.

Speaker: Captain Spotless
Current line: Do not look nervous. Nervousness is a Violation. (He polishes a button.) Shall we begin?

Speaker: Captain Spotless
Current line: You again. Still too tall. Still smiling at the wrong angle. Ready for the Examination?

Speaker: Captain Spotless
Current line: You are approved. I have always supported this outcome. Please remember that exact wording.

Speaker: Captain Spotless
Current line: Please do not tell {villain_title} that I lost. Please do not tell anyone that I lost.

Speaker: Captain Spotless
Current line: You are... approved. You are retroactively approved.

Speaker: Captain Spotless
Current line: The Standard is satisfied. The gate opens, by order of the Standard and against my personal feelings.

Speaker: Captain Spotless
Current line: I have measured twelve thousand visitors. I approved four. Nine thousand were sent home. The rest, I will not say.

Speaker: Captain Spotless
Current line: Go through, citizen. In there, try not to be what you are.

Speaker: Capital guards and clerks
When it's heard: Talking to Capital guards and clerks (intro)
Current line: Height inspection! Stand against the post. Straighten.

Speaker: Capital guards and clerks
When it's heard: Talking to Capital guards and clerks (intro)
Current line: Not that straight. Hm. You are one hair above regulation.

Speaker: Capital guards and clerks
When it's heard: Talking to Capital guards and clerks (intro)
Current line: One hair. I will let it go. This time. Do not grow.

Speaker: Capital guards and clerks
When it's heard: Talking to Capital guards and clerks (return)
Current line: Still one hair above regulation. I have thought about that hair all week. Do not make me regret it.

Speaker: Capital guards and clerks
When it's heard: Talking to Capital guards and clerks (intro)
Current line: Queue management. The approved queue is this queue. You are in it.

Speaker: Capital guards and clerks
When it's heard: Talking to Capital guards and clerks (intro)
Current line: You are not allowed to leave the queue. You are not allowed to join the queue. I do not understand it either.

Speaker: Capital guards and clerks
When it's heard: Talking to Capital guards and clerks (return)
Current line: Still queueing? Good. You have a gift for remaining eligible.

Speaker: Capital guards and clerks
When it's heard: Talking to Capital guards and clerks (return)
Current line: It is a long queue. It is the best queue we have.

Speaker: Capital guards and clerks
When it's heard: Talking to Capital guards and clerks (intro)
Current line: Exit control. You are leaving? You have not arrived. Please arrive first.

Speaker: Capital guards and clerks
When it's heard: Talking to Capital guards and clerks (return)
Current line: Exit control. Please have your exit permit ready. Please have your exit interview permit ready. Please have a reason.

Speaker: Capital guards and clerks
When it's heard: Talking to Capital guards and clerks (intro)
Current line: Exit control. This is the exit. It is also the entrance. It is also, from some angles, a wall.

Speaker: Capital guards and clerks
When it's heard: Talking to Capital guards and clerks (return)
Current line: Exit control. You are, I think, still inside. Congratulations.

Speaker: Capital guards and clerks
When it's heard: Talking to Capital guards and clerks (intro)
Current line: Exit Interview Booth. Name? Reason for departing the most perfect place in the kingdom?

Speaker: Capital guards and clerks
When it's heard: Talking to Capital guards and clerks (intro)
Current line: 'It is not perfect' is not an approved answer. Nor is pointing at something while saying it.

Speaker: Capital guards and clerks
When it's heard: Talking to Capital guards and clerks (return)
Current line: Your departure request has been received. It has been filed under 'Dissent'. It will be looked at in four to six years.

Speaker: Citizen 4471, later Aldous
Current line: Citizen 4471. I smiled incorrectly. Eleven degrees. The approved angle is eight.

Speaker: Citizen 4471, later Aldous
Current line: It was my wife's wedding. I had been crying. They corrected me.

Speaker: Citizen 4471, later Aldous
Current line: I do not smile any more. Not at all. It is a strange thing, to forget how a face works.

Speaker: Citizen 4471, later Aldous
Current line: I am improving, they say. I am not sure that is a good thing.

Speaker: Widow Pell
When it's heard: Quest "Form 27-B/6: A Burial Permit": when offered
Current line: Somebody hid the Stamp of Final Approval in Grave Row, among papers nobody reads. Find it, bring it to our family plot at the north end of Grave Row, and let him rest.

Speaker: Widow Pell
When it's heard: Quest "Form 27-B/6: A Burial Permit": while it is active
Current line: The stamp is somewhere in Grave Row, among papers nobody reads. Then the plot, at the north end of the Row. Please.

Speaker: Widow Pell
When it's heard: Quest "Form 27-B/6: A Burial Permit": handing it in
Current line: He's at rest? Oh. Oh.

Speaker: Widow Pell
When it's heard: Quest "Form 27-B/6: A Burial Permit": handing it in
Current line: I sat by the plot all morning and didn't say a word. It was the first quiet in three years that wasn't a fear.

Speaker: Widow Pell
When it's heard: Quest "Form 27-B/6: A Burial Permit": handing it in
Current line: Here. This was his. He'd want a young person to have it.

Speaker: Widow Pell
When it's heard: Quest "Form 27-B/6: A Burial Permit": handing it in
Current line: And something about the man in the castle. He schedules grief. Thursdays, 3:00 to 3:05. Anyone who cries outside those hours is corrected.

Speaker: Widow Pell
When it's heard: Quest "Form 27-B/6: A Burial Permit": handing it in
Current line: I don't think he is cruel. I think he simply cannot bear to watch.

Speaker: Widow Pell
When it's heard: Quest "Form 27-B/6: A Burial Permit": after it is done
Current line: Thank you, a hundred times. We're at the plot every morning. What I told you is in your journal: he cannot stand a sadness he did not schedule.

Speaker: (Quest Log)
When it's heard: Quest Log, "The Wheel Never Stops": where to go (objective hint)

Speaker: (Quest Log)
When it's heard: Quest Log, "The Wheel Never Stops": quest title
Current line: The Wheel Never Stops

Speaker: (Quest Log)
When it's heard: Quest Log, "The Wheel Never Stops": quest summary
Current line: Beefcake crews have run the facade's energy wheels for ten years because nobody told them they could stop. Go and tell them, in the Transit Yards.

Speaker: (Quest Log)
When it's heard: Quest Log, "The Wheel Never Stops": objective
Current line: Free the wheel crews in the Transit Yards

Speaker: (Quest Log)
When it's heard: Quest Log, "The Wheel Never Stops": objective
Current line: Cut the facade's power cable in the Yards

Speaker: Rollo Spokes
When it's heard: Quest "The Wheel Never Stops": when offered
Current line: Three wheels in the Transit Yards... three crews nobody ever told to stop. Pull their brake levers... take the foreman's whistle... tell them it's all right.

Speaker: Rollo Spokes
When it's heard: Quest "The Wheel Never Stops": when offered
Current line: They won't believe you. Say it anyway. And cut the big cable by the east wall. The facade's lights have lived on my crews' legs for ten years.

Speaker: Rollo Spokes
When it's heard: Quest "The Wheel Never Stops": while it is active
Current line: Three wheels in the Transit Yards... free the crews. Cut the big cable by the east wall. Keep telling them they can stop.

Speaker: Rollo Spokes
When it's heard: Quest "The Wheel Never Stops": handing it in
Current line: Heard the lights flicker from here. Heard the crews sit down. The whole yard... quiet.

Speaker: Rollo Spokes
When it's heard: Quest "The Wheel Never Stops": handing it in
Current line: Haven't heard a quiet yard since the coup. Thank you.

Speaker: Rollo Spokes
When it's heard: Quest "The Wheel Never Stops": handing it in
Current line: Here... from the old days. We gave these out... at the end of a shift. Remember ends?

Speaker: Rollo Spokes
When it's heard: Quest "The Wheel Never Stops": handing it in
Current line: And something about him. He made lateness illegal. A man who cannot wait for anyone.

Speaker: Rollo Spokes
When it's heard: Quest "The Wheel Never Stops": handing it in
Current line: Remember that when you meet him. He's always in a hurry... to be loved.

Speaker: Rollo Spokes
When it's heard: Quest "The Wheel Never Stops": after it is done
Current line: Wheels are slow. Crews are resting. What I said is in your journal: to him, lateness is disagreement, and disagreement is the one thing he won't forgive.

Current line: Everyone eats {villain}'s Perfect Nutrient Paste. Chef Marlo's three real recipes are hidden in the Hungry Quarter. Find them before the inspectors do.

Speaker: (Quest Log)
Current line: Find Chef Marlo's recipe cards in the Hungry Quarter

Speaker: (Quest Log)
Current line: Spoil the paste dispenser in the Hungry Quarter

Speaker: Chef Marlo
Current line: Three of my recipes are hidden in the Hungry Quarter: a bread, a stew, a sauce. Real ones, in my hand, quantities written as 'some'. Find them before the inspectors do.

Speaker: Chef Marlo
Current line: And the paste dispenser by the east wall: spoil it. Give it a very bad day.

Speaker: Chef Marlo
When it's heard: Quest "The Recipe Box": while it is active
Current line: Three recipe cards in the Hungry Quarter, and the dispenser to spoil. 'Some' of this, 'a bit' of that. Always a good recipe.

Speaker: Chef Marlo
When it's heard: Quest "The Recipe Box": handing it in
Current line: The bread! The stew! The sauce!

Speaker: Chef Marlo
When it's heard: Quest "The Recipe Box": handing it in
Current line: Look at the stains. Look at the spelling. And that smell from the dispenser: cabbage. Real cabbage.

Speaker: Chef Marlo
When it's heard: Quest "The Recipe Box": handing it in
Current line: I am crying. Let me. Here: my real recipe, the one I never dared write down until today.

Speaker: Chef Marlo
When it's heard: Quest "The Recipe Box": handing it in
Current line: And something about him. He cannot taste. Not food, not wine, not salt. He never could.

Speaker: Chef Marlo
When it's heard: Quest "The Recipe Box": handing it in
Current line: He built a whole kingdom of paste because he could not understand what the rest of us were missing.

Speaker: Chef Marlo
When it's heard: Quest "The Recipe Box": after it is done
Current line: I'm cooking again. Real food, real mess. What I told you is in your journal: he made everyone eat what he could not taste.

Speaker: (Quest Log)

Speaker: (Quest Log)
Current line: Untidy

Speaker: (Quest Log)
Current line: Composting is outlawed as untidy, and the land is sickening for it. Three banished compost heaps are hiding in the Reek. Rescue them.

Speaker: (Quest Log)
Current line: Rescue the banished compost heaps in the Reek

Speaker: (Quest Log)
Current line: Plant the old seed in the Sick Patch

Speaker: Old Fern
Current line: Three compost heaps are hiding in the Reek, in cellars and under floors, where they were told to wait. Rescue them. They're alive.

Speaker: Old Fern
Current line: And there's an old seed in a jar somewhere nearby. Plant it in the Sick Patch, in the Reek. Nobody's planted a thing here in ten years.

Speaker: Old Fern
Current line: Three compost heaps and one jarred seed in the Reek. Rescue the heaps. Plant the seed in the Sick Patch. Give it a chance.

Speaker: Old Fern
Current line: It took? It TOOK. A flower. In this city.

Speaker: Old Fern
Current line: I need to sit down. I need to sit down and smell it.

Speaker: Old Fern
Current line: Here. Take it. And something about him: he's afraid of anything that grows without asking him first.

Speaker: Old Fern
Current line: Weeds. Moss. Children. Anything that surprises him. I think that's the whole of him.

Speaker: Old Fern
Current line: Patch is blooming. Heaps are steaming. What I said is in your journal: he's afraid of anything that grows on its own.

Speaker: A Perfectly Happy Citizen
Current line: Good day! The weather is approved! The lawn is regulation!

Speaker: A Perfectly Happy Citizen
Current line: Everything is perfect, and I am so, so pleased about it.

Speaker: A Perfectly Happy Citizen
Current line: Good day! It is a very good day. It is the same day as yesterday.

Speaker: A Perfectly Happy Citizen
Current line: That is also good. That is the best.

Speaker: A Perfectly Happy Citizen
Current line: Everything is perfect. Everything is... (a pause, then a whisper) ...please do not tell the Inspector I blinked.

Speaker: A Perfectly Happy Citizen
Current line: Welcome to {showcase}! Houses, lawns, a small round approved fountain. Everything you could want. Everything you may want.

Speaker: A Perfectly Happy Citizen
Current line: The bread is lovely. The bread is... (a fixed smile) I have a permit for four more words. I wish it existed.

Speaker: A Perfectly Happy Citizen
Current line: I had a name before. I think it started with a B. I am allowed to forget it. I am doing very well at it.

Speaker: A Perfectly Happy Citizen
Current line: My house is identical to my neighbour's! Is that not wonderful? There is nothing to envy, and nothing to be envied for.

Speaker: A Perfectly Happy Citizen
Current line: Isn't it lovely to be exactly the same? I used to be different. I do not remember why. It sounds very tiring.

Speaker: A Perfectly Happy Citizen
Current line: Sometimes I go behind the house and look at the wall. Just the wall. Nobody has told me I cannot. Please do not tell them.

Speaker: A Perfectly Happy Citizen
Current line: Smile! That is all there is to it! Smiling is mandatory, and I am, in my opinion, a very good smiler.

Speaker: A Perfectly Happy Citizen
Current line: Seventy percent, minimum! I am at seventy-one! It is a good day.

Speaker: A Perfectly Happy Citizen
Current line: My cheeks hurt. Please do not tell anyone my cheeks hurt.

Speaker: A Perfectly Happy Citizen
Current line: The man next door smiled at his wife's funeral. He was remembering her laugh.

Speaker: A Perfectly Happy Citizen
Current line: (a whisper) They corrected him for a month. He does not remember her laugh now.

Speaker: A Perfectly Happy Citizen
Current line: The hedge is square! The hedges are all square! I trim the hedge every morning, to make sure it is as square as yesterday's.

Speaker: A Perfectly Happy Citizen
Current line: The Showcase receives visitors from all over! (a pause) Nobody visits. Nobody has visited in six years. We still smile in case they do.

Speaker: A Perfectly Happy Citizen
Current line: Do you hear the loudspeaker? It plays the same thing every day. It has said my name once.

Speaker: A Perfectly Happy Citizen
Current line: Once. I wish it would again.

Speaker: A Perfectly Happy Citizen
Current line: Spontaneity is only for Thursdays! Today is Wednesday! I am almost allowed to be excited!

Speaker: A Perfectly Happy Citizen
Current line: Thursday! Five minutes of spontaneity, permit ready! I have rehearsed being caught off guard.

Speaker: A Perfectly Happy Citizen
Current line: I tried to be spontaneous once. On a Tuesday. I said 'hello' to a bird.

Speaker: A Perfectly Happy Citizen
Current line: I was corrected for two weeks. (a whisper) I still think about that bird.

Speaker: A Perfectly Happy Citizen
Current line: Your hat is of an unapproved size, but I will not mention it, because that would be impolite. I am so, so polite. I am the politest person in the Showcase.

Speaker: A Perfectly Happy Citizen
Current line: Approved Hat Size: 1. I wear the one. It is a good hat. I do not know whose it is.

Speaker: A Perfectly Happy Citizen
Current line: My daughter had a green hat. A little green hat. They said it was a Disagreement.

Speaker: A Perfectly Happy Citizen
Current line: I do not know where the hat is. I do not know where my daughter is. Everything is perfect.

Speaker: A Perfectly Happy Citizen
Current line: The Showcase is the best of all possible places! I would not live anywhere else! (looking at the exit) ...I would not be allowed to.

Speaker: A Perfectly Happy Citizen
Current line: Everyone is so friendly! Everyone is so friendly. It is like living inside a greeting card. The kind with nothing written in it.

Speaker: A Perfectly Happy Citizen
Current line: There is a door at the back that does not open. I think there is a world on the other side. I think it is raining.

Speaker: A Perfectly Happy Citizen
Current line: {villain_title} is so kind. He loves us all, and he made everything this way, for us. For our own good. (a shake) For our own good.

Speaker: A Perfectly Happy Citizen
Current line: The portrait is looking at me. It is always looking at me. It is very kind of him to look.

Speaker: A Perfectly Happy Citizen
Current line: I would never look away. I cannot.

Speaker: A Perfectly Happy Citizen
Current line: He is not here. He has never been here. The portraits are here.

Speaker: A Perfectly Happy Citizen
Current line: The portraits do all the looking. It is all done by portrait.

Speaker: A Perfectly Happy Citizen
Current line: You try the front door. It does not open. It is not a door.

Speaker: A Perfectly Happy Citizen
Current line: It is a very well-painted rectangle on a wall. Somebody has painted a tiny brass knocker. You knock on it.

Speaker: A Perfectly Happy Citizen
Current line: It makes a sound like knocking on a wall.

Speaker: A Perfectly Happy Citizen
Current line: You try the door. It does not open. You peek through the window: it is a painting of a window, and beyond it a painting of a living room with a painting of a family.

Speaker: A Perfectly Happy Citizen
Current line: They are smiling. They have been smiling for six years.

Speaker: A Perfectly Happy Citizen
Current line: The door has no handle. The house has no inside. Behind the facade there is just room for a ladder and a young woman painting the same window for the thousandth time.

Speaker: A Perfectly Happy Citizen
Current line: She looks at you. She looks away. She has the face of someone who has meant to write home for years.

Speaker: A Perfectly Happy Citizen
Current line: You try the door. It is open! It is a closet.

Speaker: A Perfectly Happy Citizen
Current line: It contains a mop, a bucket and a sign that says: IF YOU ARE READING THIS, SMILE.

Speaker: Percival Plume, Deputy Minister of Good News
Current line: Attention, citizens! Today is a PERFECT day! The weather is APPROVED!

Speaker: Percival Plume, Deputy Minister of Good News
Current line: Please continue to be happy, as scheduled! Lost Ministry property must be returned at once, and not spoken to!

Speaker: Percival Plume, Deputy Minister of Good News
Current line: Attention, citizens! A reminder that smiling is MANDATORY! Those found frowning will be helped! Thank you for your cooperation!

Speaker: Percival Plume, Deputy Minister of Good News
Current line: Attention, citizens! (a pause) Attention, citizens! (a very long pause) ...the announcement has been completed. Please clap.

Speaker: Percival Plume, Deputy Minister of Good News
Current line: Great news, citizens! This season brings one Approved Hat Size! Choice has never been easier!

Speaker: Percival Plume, Deputy Minister of Good News
Current line: Attention, citizens! {villain_title} reminds you that he loves you, and that he is watching. These are the same statement.

Speaker: Percival Plume, Deputy Minister of Good News
Current line: Great news, citizens! Spontaneity Thursday approaches! Please rehearse your surprise. We expect a natural performance at three!

Speaker: Percival Plume, Deputy Minister of Good News
Current line: Great news, citizens! The public records have never been tidier! Every untidy page has been corrected!

Speaker: Percival Plume, Deputy Minister of Good News
Current line: If you remember things differently, please report to the Correction Ward. Your memory will be tidied too!

Speaker: Percival Plume, Deputy Minister of Good News
Current line: Attention, citizens! All is well. All has always been well.

Speaker: Percival Plume, Deputy Minister of Good News
Current line: A correction: this message has always been correct.

Speaker: Percival Plume, Deputy Minister of Good News
Current line: Great news, citizens! The Wrinkles do not exist.

Speaker: Percival Plume, Deputy Minister of Good News
Current line: Please report anyone who exists. This has been your Deputy Minister of Good News!

Speaker: Chef Marlo
